plotSections.title: Echoes and Ledzbika
bullets: Ord recalls two spirit encounters: a hostile man who disliked the party and wanted to give something back to Sylan, and a frightened woman who wanted help and did not want to go back. When struck, the spirits became tangible and started changing.

The elderly male is remembered as a high elf, Ledzbika. He named his neighbor Claire Belle and accused her of trying to steal his belongings. A possible name Hofford was mentioned and dismissed as unimportant.
Ledzbika died about a month ago of natural causes and did not return as one of the town's echoes. The speaker calls that the head-scratcher.

The speaker distinguishes celestial echoes from undead: echoes are celestial forms of the dead, while spirits fall under undead. A portal the party opened into another dimension is cited as evidence these beings were not corporeal.

Former residents and travelers of the town, from when it was simply Neville, escaped without realizing it was a prison. On death they could die normally or return as a celestial echo of themselves. The account is hedged as coming from a drunk girl and is guessed to involve a sea-related elder god, heard as Taquil, and some unclear consequence of using that being.

That arrangement is given as the reason the town is not full of rampant undead. Over the last six or seven months there have been a handful of deaths, about a half dozen and maybe as many as a dozen, plus unknown travelers.
Sylan worries he has failed a duty to travel and find lost souls, or that New Navel traps souls. He decides the echoes may be a separate matter, worth investigating later, but not now.

plotSections.title: The sheriff's terms
bullets: Summoning undead is against town rules. Sylan is told to keep the lantern hidden or it will be confiscated, and he agrees.
The party plans to have dinner, make plans, and leave soon on a mission. Asked if something has come up, the speaker says Gerk will explain, then leaves that explanation unmade.

They are told to keep a companion, heard as a jug or dragon friend, away from the ghosts, and to use no doors in town. An exception for the tavern is withdrawn: friends may open ordinary doors, but they are to walk in. Gerk's offer to use only windows is refused for lack of paperwork.
They are told to keep commotion outside town. The speaker moseys back to the porch. Gerk understands this as an order to stay out of town.

plotSections.title: The helm at the lighthouse
bullets: Before leaving the street, Gerk shows Sylan a wicker chicken he bought for one gold. Sylan thinks it well made. Gerk alludes to other creatures he has not killed yet; Sylan offers to buy them and then starts for Shades and Trades the long way through town to check he missed no one.
Gerk says Carlkin wants them arrested. Sylan jokes that court is politics, only slower. The scene is paused before that is resolved.

At the lighthouse, Carlkin has been measuring the helm and grinding reagents in a mortar. He mixes them with a brackish, pond-like liquid, shakes a two-to-three-ounce vial until it turns crystal clear, and calls the result a soul identifier: a finer reading than the bag.
He says the helm is not a phylactery. A phylactery would have blown up, burst into flames, and possibly provoked a magical reaction.

A drop of the liquid sticks and pools on the helm instead of running off. Through a magnifying glass, Carlkin finds spiritual residue and asks whether Walker interacted with the helm spiritually when he picked it up.
Walker says that after he killed the emperor they had a conversation, and that the emperor was different. The explanation is cut off while the group is checking whether Walker already told them.

chronologicalEvents: Ord recounts a hostile male spirit who wanted to give something back to Sylan and a frightened woman who wanted help and refused to go back; striking the spirits made them tangible and they began to change.
The elderly male spirit is identified as Ledzbika, a high elf who accused his neighbor Claire Belle of stealing from him. Hofford is floated as a name and set aside.
Ledzbika is said to have died of natural causes about a month ago and not to have returned as an echo.

Echoes are explained as celestial returns of the dead, distinct from undead and spirits. The town's dead could choose a normal death or a celestial echo after escaping a prison they had not recognized, under an uncertain sea-god influence.
Recent local deaths are put at roughly a half dozen to a dozen over six or seven months, with mines reopening across the lake and heavy traveler traffic.
Sylan raises soul-trapping versus his duty to lost souls, then sets the question aside. He agrees to conceal the lantern after being warned that summoning undead is illegal.
The party says it will eat, plan, and leave soon. The speaker defers to Gerk, bans doors and ghost-trouble, rejects window travel, and returns to the porch.
Gerk shows the one-gold wicker chicken. Sylan starts the long way toward Shades and Trades. Gerk says they were told to stay out of town and that Carlkin wants them arrested.
The scene shifts to Carlkin finishing a soul identifier and applying it to the helm. The helm is not a phylactery, but the reagent beads on it and shows spiritual residue.
Walker says he spoke with the emperor after killing him and that the emperor was different. The talk is interrupted before it is finished.

Ledzbika.existing: Elderly half-elf spirit pulled from rest, trying to return to his abode.
notes: Remembered here as an elderly high elf male.
Died about a month ago of natural causes.
Accused his neighbor Claire Belle of trying to steal his belongings; his rants are what the speaker remembers.
Did not return as a celestial echo, unlike others who died in town.
Likely the hostile spirit who disliked the party and wanted to give something back to Sylan. The spirits became somewhat tangible when struck and started changing.
personality: Remembered for his rants and hostility toward the party.
openQuestions: Why Ledzbika did not return as a celestial echo.

Claire Belle.existing: The neighbor Ledzbika accuses of stealing his family's silver.
notes: Ledzbika named her as his neighbor and said she was trying to steal his things.

Haldor.existing: Sheriff of New Navel who bans doors and spirit-taking inside the city.
notes: The town speaker, addressed afterward by Gerk as Howdy, confirms Ledzbika's death and the echo rules, then returns to a porch.
He orders the lantern kept hidden or confiscated because summoning undead is illegal.
He forbids doors in town, including into the tavern, and tells them to have friends open ordinary doors and otherwise walk in. He refuses Gerk's windows-only joke for lack of paperwork.

He tells them to keep a companion heard as a jug or dragon friend away from the ghosts, keep commotion outside town, and says Gerk will explain whatever has come up. He leaves before that explanation happens.
Gerk takes the exchange as an instruction to stay out of town.
personality: Enforces the town bans on doors and undead, and shuts down loopholes.
quotesThemes: Echoes are celestials; undead are undead, and spirits fall under undead.
Summoning undead is against town rules.
openQuestions: What he expected Gerk to explain.

notes: He is concerned that he has not fulfilled a duty to travel and find lost souls, or that New Navel traps souls. He sets the celestial echoes aside for lack of time.
He agrees to keep the lantern under wraps and accepts the ban on doors.
The party will have dinner, plan, and leave soon because they are on a mission.
He plans to take the long way through town to Shades and Trades to be sure he missed no one. The walk is interrupted by the cut back to the lighthouse.
He treats Gerk's claim that Carlkin wants them arrested as a possible court matter and compares court to slower politics.
personality: Treats searching out lost souls as a personal duty, but will not delay the current mission for the echo question.
quotesThemes: Either he has failed to find lost souls, or New Navel has a way of trapping them.
openQuestions: Whether New Navel traps souls or his search for lost souls is unfinished.

Gerk.existing: Half-orc barbarian, Doorman, and Child of the Great Eldarin Tree.
notes: He shows Sylan a wicker chicken bought for one gold and says there are also other creatures he has not killed yet.
He answers the door ban by offering to use only windows.
He believes the sheriff told him to stay out of town and to keep a companion away from the ghosts.
He says Carlkin wants them arrested. That situation is paused.
openQuestions: Whether Carlkin actually wants the party arrested.

Walker.existing: Half-elf dragon rider and fighter bonded to Glimmen.
notes: Carlkin directs the helm reading at him because of spiritual residue from when Walker picked the helm up.
Walker says that after he killed the emperor, they had a conversation, and that the emperor was different.
He thinks he may already have explained this to the group. The explanation is cut off.
openQuestions: What Walker and the emperor said, and in what way the emperor was different.

Carlkin.existing: Turtle-like person believed to be back in Langdale; examines the helm by appointment.
notes: At the lighthouse he measures the helm, grinds reagents, and mixes them with a brackish liquid that turns clear in a two-to-three-ounce vial.
He identifies the result as a soul identifier, a finer reading than the bag, and finds spiritual residue on the helm.
He rules out a phylactery: one would have blown up, burst into flames, and possibly caused a magical reaction.
Gerk claims Carlkin wants the party arrested. The claim is not confirmed before the scene is paused.
personality: Works through the test aloud and checks who already knows Walker's story before continuing.
quotesThemes: The helm is definitely not a phylactery.
There is spiritual residue attached to the helm.
openQuestions: Whether Carlkin wants the party arrested.

notes: Walker says he talked with the emperor after killing him, in connection with picking up the helm.
Walker says the emperor was different during that contact. No further description is given before the chunk ends.
openQuestions: Who the emperor is, and how he was different when Walker spoke with him.

notes: One of the spirits the party met. She was scared, wanted help, and did not want to go back.
Like the other spirit, she became tangible when struck and started changing.

New Navel.existing: Familiar stop that sends trade caravans to the party's tavern in Langdale and holds Carlkin's lighthouse.
notes: Described as a frontier town with all sorts of residents and travelers. Mines on the other side of the lake are opening again and drawing competition.
Roughly a half dozen to a dozen deaths in the last six or seven months, plus unknown traveler deaths.
Summoning undead is illegal, magical doors are banned, and the lantern must stay hidden. Commotion is supposed to stay outside town.
Sylan suspects the town may trap souls. He also thinks the celestial echoes may be a separate mystery.

Old Navel.existing: A place Ord and Sylan name as the source of spirits the party stirred by walking past.
notes: The town was known as Neville before it was New Navel. Its residents and travelers later said they had escaped without realizing they were in a prison.
Those who died could return as celestial echoes of themselves. Ledzbika's failure to do so is singled out as unexplained.

Celestial echo.existing: New Navel's dead who return as celestial forms of themselves, not ghosts or undead.
notes: Restated against ghosts and undead: echoes are celestials, undead are undead, and spirits fall under undead.
The choice to return was available to people who died after escaping the old town's prison. A normal death was the other option.
The story is attributed uncertainly to a drunk girl and possibly to a sea-related elder god.
The same arrangement is offered as the reason echoes are discussed alongside undead and why the city is not overrun by undead.
The spirits the party struck became tangible and began to change. A portal into another dimension is used as evidence they were not corporeal.
openQuestions: Why Ledzbika did not come back as an echo.

Helm.existing: A helm Carlkin agreed to examine by appointment once a comrade returns.
notes: Carlkin is measuring it at the lighthouse and tests it with a soul identifier.
It is not a phylactery.
The reagent pools where it lands instead of running off. Carlkin reads spiritual residue on it.
The residue is tied to Walker picking it up and to Walker's conversation with the emperor after killing him.
openQuestions: What the spiritual residue records about Walker and the emperor.

Soul identifier.existing: Carlkin's reagent for a finer reading of an object's spiritual residue.
notes: Carlkin makes it on the spot: ground reagents mixed with a brackish, pond-water-like liquid, shaken clear in a two-to-three-ounce vial.
He compares it to the bag and says it gives a finer reading.
One drop sits and pools on the helm. Examined with a magnifying glass, it shows spiritual residue.

Fused lantern-staff.existing: Fused lantern and staff that reveals the Ethereal Plane and draws nearby spirits when the active staff is held.
notes: The town speaker orders this lantern kept under wraps because summoning undead is illegal, and threatens to confiscate it. Sylan agrees.

Door.existing: A door that stretches reality between places.
notes: Doors are forbidden in town. A brief allowance for a door into the tavern is withdrawn.
Ordinary entry is to be opened by friends or done on foot. Gerk's proposal to travel by windows is rejected.
